variations.notes: Played on the ganga (gunga). Media plays off of ganga.
Played on the medio. The tim is a strong/filled preso (▲), played before the tom.
Played on the viola. Related to angolinha.

glossary.english: the single-string musical bow that leads capoeira music
the largest, lowest-pitched berimbau; keeps the base rhythm (also written 'ganga')
the medium-pitched berimbau; plays the counter-rhythm
'jump/leap'; the open low tone (notation down-triangle, syllable 'tom')
the buzzed/scratched sound made when the dobrao rests lightly on the string (notation X, syllable 'chi')
'pressed/held'; the high tone made by pressing the dobrao against the string (notation up-triangle, syllable 'tim')
the coin or stone pressed against the berimbau string to change pitch
the woven rattle held together with the playing stick
a slower, lower style of capoeira, and its berimbau toque
'little Angola'; a variation toque related to Angola do brada
the gunga's base-rhythm role that the other berimbaus play off of

instructions.text: Cue the berimbau to your voice (sing the rhythm, then match the bow to it).
Use do-re-mi-fa-si as a guide and pull the string with a finger to shift the tone.
Start with the gunga, then layer the medio and viola off of its ganga.
Pick the mestre's register that is easy for you to sing along with.
gunga's up-triangle (tim) equals the medio's salto (tom) in pitch terms.

culture.text: The berimbau leads the roda: the gunga sets the base, the medio answers, and the viola improvises on top.
Angola is the older, slower, closer-to-the-ground style; its toques (Angola, Angola do brada, angolinha) carry that feel.
